topics.title: Linear Algebra
topics.syllabus: Vector space, basis, linear dependence and independence, matrix algebra, eigen values and eigen vectors, rank, solution of linear equations - existence and uniqueness.

topics.title: Calculus
topics.syllabus: Mean value theorems, theorems of integral calculus, evaluation of definite and improper integrals, partial derivatives, maxima and minima, multiple integrals, line, surface and volume integrals, Taylor series.

topics.title: Probability and Statistics
topics.syllabus: Mean, median, mode, standard deviation, combinatorial probability, probability distributions, binomial distribution, Poisson distribution, exponential distribution, normal distribution, joint and conditional probability.

cards.title: Conditional probability and Bayes
cards.bodyHtml: When a test or a witness is described as accurate some percentage of the time, the base rate usually dominates the answer. A rare event reported by a good detector is still most often a false alarm.
cards.pitfallHtml: Answering with the detector's accuracy and ignoring the prior is exactly the trap these questions are built around.

cards.title: Mean, variance and expectation
cards.bodyHtml: Expectation is linear whether or not the variables are independent; variance adds only when they are uncorrelated.

cards.bodyHtml: For identically distributed continuous variables, questions like P(X<Y)P(X<Y)P(X<Y) need no integration — the labels are interchangeable and ties have probability zero.

cards.title: Median, mode, spread and counting
cards.bodyHtml: Mean, median and mode coincide only for a symmetric unimodal distribution — a question that gives all three different is telling you the data is skewed. Standard deviation is almost always faster computed as x2‾−xˉ2\overline{x^2}-\bar x^2x2−xˉ2 than from the definition.
cards.pitfallHtml: A set can have no mode, or several. And the median of a distribution solves F(m)=0.5F(m)=0.5F(m)=0.5 — for an exponential that is ln⁡2/λ\ln2/\lambdaln2/λ, not 1/λ1/\lambda1/λ.
